proof: For $n=1$, the empty sample already leaves at most one concept, so the value is zero. Let $n\ge2$. For the all-zero labeling, a sample of $s$ zero coordinates leaves exactly $n-s$ singleton concepts. Thus at least $n-1$ coordinates are needed to leave at most one, and $n-1$ suffice. For any labeling with a positive coordinate $i$, the single example $(i,1)$ leaves exactly the singleton $\{i\}$ consistent with the sample, even if the full labeling has other positive coordinates. This meets the definition, which asks for at most one consistent concept rather than identification of the possibly unrealizable labeling. Hence every such labeling has specifying size at most one, and the maximum is $n-1$.
name: Extended Teaching Dimension of Singletons
